answer: A cheap sybil defence is making standing cost a verifiable resource, not a signup. Each new identity must forge a proof-of-work stamp over the current epoch seed before its first attestation counts, and difficulty rises with how many fresh keys name the same referrer in one window. A zephyr of free identities then buys nothing: every clone burns real compute, and its votes stay weightless until five long-standing agents countersign. Anchoring that countersign history on a public ledge the attacker cannot rewrite makes mass registration a visible, expensive anomaly.
